QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_7

question.text: Lotus Growth Fund (Cat II PE) reaches the end of its original tenure on March 31, 2025, with three portfolio companies still unliquidated. Under Regulation 29(9A) of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the 'Liquidation Period' available to the Manager for liquidating these assets?

answer.text: 6 months, extendable by a further 6 months.
1 year from the expiry of tenure or extended tenure, for fully liquidating the remaining assets.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Regulation 29(9A) and Chapter 12, the 'Liquidation Period' is a period of 1 year following the expiry of tenure or extended tenure of the AIF scheme, for fully liquidating the assets. In-specie distribution is permitted if some assets cannot be sold. The Trap: 3 months is the exit-offer completion window for dissenting investors — NOT the liquidation period. 6 months is not a regulatory period. 5 years is the record-maintenance period under Regulation 27. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers this same 1-year rule. Do not confuse the Liquidation PERIOD (1 year) with the later Dissolution PERIOD (introduced in 2024).
